because a letter had arrived from the greater Sultan,
namely, the Caliph.
And when Chagri Beg was insisting,
Tughril Beg took a knife and said,
"I will kill myself,
if you do this."
And then he ceased,
after he had taken from the inhabitants of the city five hundred thousand zuzes.
And Tughril Beg wrote an answer to the Caliph thus:
"From his servant and his subject, Tughril Beg son of Michael."
And Qizil, their brother-in-law,
that is, the husband of their sister, also wrote:
"From his servant and his minister, Qizil son of Yahya."
Chagri Beg, however, did not write anything.
And Tughril Beg entered Nishapur,
and sat upon the throne of Sultan Mas'ud.
And Chagri Beg resided in the city of Sarakhs,
and Qizil in Rayy the city.
And in the year 430
430 of the Arabs [1038-1039 CE],
snow fell in Baghdad,
and it stood about a span deep,
and it remained for days in the streets.
And after it, in Kanun, there was severe cold,
and the waters froze for six days.
And in this year, Sultan Mas'ud gathered numerous armies from Inner Persia and Outer India,
and came against the Ghuzz,
and defeated them near Marw al-Rudh.
And about three thousand and five hundred men of them were killed,
and the rest, with their leaders Tughril Beg and Chagri Beg, fled to the desolate desert.
And Sultan Mas'ud resided in the region of Khurasan for about two years.
And then he left forces in the region itself,
and he himself returned and went to Ghazna, the city of Khwarazm {OCR? Ghazna/Khwarazm conflation}.
And when the Ghuzz heard this,
they came again to Khurasan in the year 432
432 of the Arabs [1040-1041 CE].
And those who were there were unable to stand before them,
and they ruled over it and over Azerbaijan.
And in this year the Romans went out to Syria,
and the Emir Anushtekin met them near Hama,
and defeated them,
and captured the cousin of the king,
and killed an important eunuch.
And in this year, when Sultan Mas'ud set out for the land of India during the winter time, as was the custom,
because of the severity of the cold of the land of Khwarazm {Ghazna?},
